name: org.machanism.machai:project-layout
description: Project Layout is a Java utility library for detecting, describing, and processing conventional project directory layouts. It provides a common abstraction for source roots, test roots, resources, documentation folders, modules, and project identifiers so build tooling, scanners, generators, validation utilities, documentation tooling, indexing systems, and plugins can work with heterogeneous repositories without hard-coding ecosystem-specific path conventions. The artifact supports Maven projects through org.machanism.machai.project.layout.MavenProjectLayout and PomReader, Gradle projects through org.machanism.machai.project.layout.GradleProjectLayout, JavaScript and TypeScript package workspaces through org.machanism.machai.project.layout.JScriptProjectLayout, Python project detection through org.machanism.machai.project.layout.PythonProjectLayout, and fallback filesystem inspection through org.machanism.machai.project.layout.DefaultProjectLayout. ProjectLayoutManager selects the appropriate layout implementation for a project root, while ProjectProcessor provides a base workflow for scanning modules or processing a single project folder. This library is useful when building Maven or Gradle plugins, repository analyzers, source-code generators, documentation publishers, validation tools, and semantic indexing pipelines that need consistent root-relative project structure discovery on Java 8 or later.

usageContext: Detect Maven, Gradle, JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, or fallback project layouts from a filesystem project root
Resolve root-relative production source, test source, resource, and documentation directories for tooling workflows
Scan single-module and multi-module repositories and delegate folder processing to custom processors
Read Maven pom.xml metadata and derive Maven module, source, test, and documentation conventions
Support build plugins, repository analyzers, documentation generators, validation utilities, and indexing pipelines

constructors.description: Creates a Maven project layout resolver that reads pom.xml metadata to discover modules, source directories, resources, test directories, and documentation roots. Configure it with projectDir(java.io.File) before calling accessors.

examples.description: Creates and configures a Maven layout resolver for a project root, then reads root-relative source and test directories. Use this in a Maven-aware scanner or generator before walking source files.

constructors.description: Creates a Gradle project layout resolver that uses the Gradle Tooling API to inspect a Gradle project and expose child modules plus conventional src/main, src/test, and src/site directories.

examples.description: Creates a Gradle layout resolver, points it at a Gradle root directory, and retrieves module and documentation paths for build-tool integration.

constructors.description: Creates a lightweight fallback layout resolver. It treats immediate non-excluded subdirectories of the configured project root as potential modules and returns empty source, test, and documentation lists.

examples.description: Uses the fallback resolver when no build metadata is available, allowing a tool to continue with basic directory discovery.

features.name: detectProjectLayout
features.signature: public static org.machanism.machai.project.layout.ProjectLayout detectProjectLayout(java.io.File projectDir) throws java.io.FileNotFoundException
features.description: Detects the appropriate project layout implementation for a filesystem directory. The manager supports Maven, Node.js package.json projects, Python projects, and a default fallback layout, returning a ProjectLayout configured for downstream source, test, document, and module discovery.

examples.description: Automatically detects the target project's layout and retrieves source and test paths without the caller needing to know whether the repository is Maven, JavaScript, Python, or another layout.

features.name: getSources
features.description: Returns root-relative production source and resource directories for the configured project layout. MavenProjectLayout derives values from the Maven build section and Maven defaults, while GradleProjectLayout returns conventional Gradle source roots.

examples.description: Resolves each root-relative source directory against the project root so a scanner can walk production files safely.

features.name: getModules
features.description: Returns module directories or module names for multi-module projects. MavenProjectLayout reads modules declared in pom.xml for parent POM projects, GradleProjectLayout returns child project names, JScriptProjectLayout reads package.json workspaces, and DefaultProjectLayout inspects immediate subdirectories.

examples.description: Discovers modules in a repository before processing each module independently in a build plugin or repository analyzer.

features.name: scanFolder
features.signature: public void scanFolder(java.io.File projectDir) throws java.io.IOException
features.description: Scans a project root, detects its layout, processes each declared module when modules are present, or processes the entire folder as a single project. Subclasses implement processFolder(org.machanism.machai.project.layout.ProjectLayout) to define custom behavior.

examples.description: Creates a custom processor that prints documentation directories for each detected module or project folder. This is a practical pattern for documentation publishing, validation, or indexing tools.

features.name: isMavenProject
features.description: Checks whether a directory appears to be a Maven project by looking for a pom.xml file. This is useful when a tool wants to branch explicitly before constructing MavenProjectLayout.

examples.description: Checks for Maven metadata, then creates a Maven-specific layout resolver and prints the artifactId.

features.name: getProjectModel
features.description: Loads and returns an Apache Maven Model from a pom.xml file after applying property substitutions handled by PomReader. This supports tools that need artifact metadata, build configuration, modules, or project identifiers.

examples.description: Reads Maven project metadata from pom.xml so a generator or indexer can use artifactId and display name.

customizations.name: org.machanism.machai.project.ProjectProcessor.processFolder
customizations.description: Subclass ProjectProcessor and implement processFolder(org.machanism.machai.project.layout.ProjectLayout) to define custom processing for each detected project folder or module. This extension point is suitable for scanners, documentation builders, validators, generators, and indexers.

examples.description: Defines a custom processor that consumes documentation roots from each detected layout.

customizations.name: org.machanism.machai.project.layout.ProjectLayout
customizations.description: Extend ProjectLayout to support additional ecosystems or organization-specific directory conventions by implementing getSources(), getDocuments(), and getTests(), and optionally overriding getModules(), getProjectId(), getProjectName(), and getParentId().

examples.description: Implements a custom layout for a non-standard repository while preserving the common ProjectLayout API.

studs.name: org.machanism.machai.project.layout.ProjectLayout
studs.description: Base abstraction that defines boundary methods for project layout implementations, including source, document, test, module, project name, and project id discovery. Concrete classes include MavenProjectLayout, GradleProjectLayout, JScriptProjectLayout, PythonProjectLayout, and DefaultProjectLayout.

examples.snippet:
org.machanism.machai.project.layout.ProjectLayout layout = new org.machanism.machai.project.layout.MavenProjectLayout().projectDir(new java.io.File("C:/workspace/project"));
java.lang.String layoutType = layout.getProjectLayoutType();
examples.description: Uses the abstract ProjectLayout type while relying on a concrete Maven implementation, allowing tooling code to remain implementation-neutral.

studs.name: org.machanism.machai.project.ProjectProcessor
studs.description: Base scanning workflow that detects project layouts, traverses modules, and delegates concrete folder handling to subclass implementations of processFolder.

examples.description: Creates an anonymous ProjectProcessor implementation that can be run against a project root to print discovered project identifiers.

examples.title: Install Project Layout in a Maven project
steps: Open the pom.xml of the Java tool, Maven plugin, scanner, or generator that needs project-structure discovery.
Run mvn clean verify to resolve the dependency and compile your integration.
examples.description: This scenario installs the library from Maven Central so a Java application or build plugin can call the ProjectLayout API.

examples.title: Automatically detect and use a project layout
steps: Create a java.io.File pointing to the repository or module root to inspect.
Read sources, tests, documents, and modules from the returned org.machanism.machai.project.layout.ProjectLayout.
Resolve returned root-relative paths against layout.getProjectDir() before accessing files.
examples.description: A practical how-to-use scenario for scanners or generators that should support multiple repository types with one API.

examples.title: Build a custom repository processor
steps: Add project-layout as a Maven dependency.
Subclass org.machanism.machai.project.ProjectProcessor or create an anonymous implementation.
Call scanFolder(java.io.File) with the repository root. The processor will process modules when they are detected, otherwise it will process the root folder.
examples.description: This scenario shows how to run real-world processing over a single project or multi-module repository while keeping the processor independent of Maven, Gradle, JavaScript, or Python layout details.
